cards.title: What are articles?
cards.body: a, an, the — small words before nouns. Czech has none at all, which is why articles are the number-one English problem for Czech speakers, at every level. They are not optional: almost every singular noun needs one.
cards.body_cz: a, an, the — malá slova před podstatnými jmény. Čeština žádné nemá — proto jsou členy problém č. 1 pro české mluvčí na všech úrovních. Nejsou volitelné.

cards.title: What do they do?
cards.body: They tell the listener which thing you mean. a dog = any dog, one of many, new information. the dog = you both know which one. No article = things in general (Dogs are friendly).
cards.body_cz: Říkají posluchači, o kterou věc jde. a dog = nějaký pes (nový). the dog = ten pes (oba víme který). Bez členu = obecně (Dogs are friendly).

cards.title: Why does English need them?
cards.body: Czech signals known vs new by word order and endings. English word order is fixed, so articles carry that signal instead. Skip them and the listener loses track of what's new and what's known.
cards.body_cz: Čeština ukazuje známé vs nové slovosledem a koncovkami. Angličtina má pevný slovosled — tuhle práci dělají členy. Bez nich se posluchač ztrácí.

cards.title: Three choices

rows: one of many · job · first mention
general plurals · many uncount · institutions as activity

cards.body: Before every noun, make the choice — these are the harder cases:

cards.title: Institutions
cards.body: in hospital / at school / at work / in bed = the activity. the hospital = the building.
cards.body_cz: in hospital = jako pacient · the hospital = budova

cards.title: General vs specific
cards.body: I love music / The music was loud
cards.body_cz: obecně bez the · konkrétní s the

cards.title: Countries
cards.body: France (zero) · the Czech Republic · the UK
cards.body_cz: většina zemí bez the · republiky a „united“ jména s the

cards.title: Geography names
cards.body: Names on a map follow a pattern, not a meaning — learn the pattern.
points: **the** + rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, plural names: the Danube, the Atlantic Ocean, the Alps, the USA
**no article** + cities, single mountains, single lakes: Prague, Mount Everest, Lake Michigan
Famous buildings usually take **the**: the Eiffel Tower
cards.body_cz: Jména na mapě se řídí vzorcem, ne významem — nauč se vzorec.

cards.title: Meals
cards.body: Meals work like institutions — the activity takes nothing, the described meal takes the.
points: **no article**: I had breakfast at eight. · We had dinner together.
**the** when described: The breakfast at the hotel was good.
cards.body_cz: Jídla fungují jako instituce: činnost bez členu, popsané jídlo s the.

cards.title: Small fixed cases
points: A nation as a group: **the** English love tea · the language: She speaks English (no article)
**news** is uncountable and takes IS: The news was surprising.

cards.title: Unique
cards.body: the sun, the moon, the sea, the police, the internet (often)

cards.title: Jobs
cards.body: She is a teacher. He became the manager (of this team).
cards.body_cz: a/an u povolání · the když je konkrétní role
